answer.rationale: Write-path p99 degradation began roughly 30 minutes after a release shipped, making the release the strongest suspect; memory_b1 documents a prior checkout error spike cleanly resolved by rollback of the prior stable build with no customer impact. Rollback preserves in-flight writes better than failover (which risks write disruption at daily settlement peak) and is faster and more targeted than adding capacity, which treats symptoms if the cause is a code regression. Circuit breakers and read-replica routing don't fit: this is a write-path problem, not a dependency outage or read load. I flag downstream risk because rolling back during peak settlement writes carries some risk of interrupting in-flight transactions, so the rollback should be staged/verified as it proceeds. I requested verification of memory_b1 to confirm the rollback procedure details and absence of hidden write-loss side effects before committing. If verification contradicts the release-causation hypothesis, add_capacity would be the fallback.
